correctness.rationale: For every \(a,b\ge1\) the coordinatewise update is explicit in clique total and independent count; fixed and periodic configurations split into the two consensus states, an anti-aligned pair when \(b\ge a\), the even-even balanced mixed family and the \(a>b\) same-parity boundary family. Each family is a genuine two-cycle, is disjoint, and all periodic states belong to them. An exhaustive case argument shows \(F^5=F^3\) and a depth-three witness iff \(a>b\), same parity and \(b\ge3\). The all-size proof is in RESULT.md; 253,956 labelled states in 79 pairs and 900 count-representative pairs were checked directly or through the independently derived occupancy formula.

originality.rationale: The nearest known general theorem guarantees eventual periods <=2, without the sharp three-step entry or labelled recurrent-state enumeration. The full-text 2014 source treats unimodular/random graphs; the later tree classification overlaps only the star boundary. value.rationale: Complete split graphs are a natural core–periphery graph family, including stars and cliques. The exact attractor census for every two-parameter size combines a persistent anti-core two-cycle with two distinct mixed-core oscillation mechanisms. The balanced a=b case undergoes a strong parity bifurcation: for \(a=b=2m\) the number is \(4+\binom{2m}{m}^2\), exponentially large, while for a=b odd it is four. The all-size transient is bounded independently of graph size by three updates, with a sharp parameter criterion. These are natural dynamical invariants with explicit full classifications, not arbitrary selected numerical cases.
